distractors.reason: 'Much' goes with verbs or uncountable nouns (thank you very much, much money), not directly before an adjective. We don't say 'much sorry'.
'Big' is an adjective, not an adverb of degree, so it cannot modify another adjective. We don't say 'big sorry'.
'Many' is used with plural countable nouns (many books). It never modifies an adjective like 'sorry'.

l1_interference: Falantes de português costumam traduzir 'muito' como 'much' e dizer 'much sorry'. Em inglês, usa-se 'very' antes de adjetivos como 'sorry', 'happy' ou 'tired'; 'much' é usado com verbos, como em 'thank you very much'.
explanation: In English, 'very' is the standard degree adverb before an adjective. 'Very sorry' is a common way to apologise politely, and it is stronger than just 'sorry'.

related_collocations.example: I am very happy to see you.
I am really sorry I am late.
I am very thankful for your help.

memory_tip: VERY + adjective (very sorry, very happy) | MUCH + verb or uncountable noun (thank you very much, much time)
